properties.name: A Verification has somewhere to put its evidence that is not its title, and a self-contradictory result cannot read as passing
properties.statement:
A Verification must have a durable place for what a check FOUND, separate from what the check IS — so evidence stops being written into the title, and so a result can be read by something other than a human eye.

⭐ THREE INDEPENDENT RECORDS OF ONE ROOT, which is why this is a requirement and not a style note. The near-duplicate guard surfaced a THIRD: `fact:defect-a-finding-has-no-bounds-so-grading-goes-in-the-name` was already in this design before today, saying the same thing about grading. Both facts the guard named are OBSERVATIONS on different days; this is the INTENT that answers them.

MEASURED on reflow2's own graph, 2026-08-16: 160 Verifications, MEDIAN `name` LENGTH 79.5 WORDS, 72 over 100, 17 over 300, longest 654. A `name` is what a list renders; these are reports.

THE TWO FLEET REPORTS:
(a) 2026-08-07 — a Verification held a self-contradictory result and stayed `passing` forever, because THE RESULT IS FREE TEXT. It recorded "EXIT 0, verdict 'STALE — 4 of 11'"; the tool's true exit was 1 and its source is `return 1 if stale else 0`, so `EXIT 0` meant the exact opposite of the verdict beside it. `status` is structured; the evidence is prose, and nothing in the loop can notice the disagreement.
(b) 2026-08-08 — `loop_status` is documented as "one cheap call" and is cheap to CALL and expensive to READ: `verifications.attention[0].name` came back as a single ~450-word paragraph holding a full graded walk report. Their diagnosis is the requirement: "workers write the full report into the `name` because there is no other durable place for it on the node — A MISSING FIELD BEING PAID FOR IN EVERY FUTURE READ OF THAT NODE."

⚠️ AND I AM THE LARGEST SINGLE CONTRIBUTOR. Four of the six Verifications written on 2026-08-16 exceed 300 words, and `ver:a-claim-reads-back-with-its-age` at 435 words is the FIFTH LONGEST IN THE DESIGN. I was not working around a limitation I had noticed; I had not noticed it.

WHY IT IS MORE THAN STYLE: the cheapest call in the surface, the one every worker is told to make routinely including before finishing, returns a payload dominated by prose nobody asked for. A cheap call that is expensive to read is a call people stop making — the same signal-trained-to-be-ignored failure `req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes` was built to end, arriving through a different door.

THEIR TWO ASKS: give Verification a `findings` / `report` property; and truncate `name` in `loop_status`'s rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately.

⚠️ THE LOAD-BEARING UNCERTAINTY, to answer BEFORE building: WOULD A NEW FIELD ALONE CHANGE ANYTHING? A declared field nobody writes to leaves the corpus exactly as it is — precisely the trap `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch` documented, where 112 nodes wrote an undeclared property because the declared route did not fit. And the 160 existing names cannot be migrated cleanly, because a property once written cannot be removed — the best available repair writes evidence to the new field and SHORTENS the name, duplicating rather than moving. Truncating at the rollup is the cheaper half and asks nobody to change how they write; whether that is pragmatic or merely lets the hoard grow unchecked is unmeasured.
